title: Mistral Releases Open Weights for Mistral Large 4, a 1-Trillion-Parameter Model, With API at $0.70/$2.10
summary: On October 29 Mistral AI published the weights of Mistral Large 4 on Hugging Face. The 1-trillion-parameter model, with about 52 billion parameters active per token, ships under a modified MIT licence that is free for commercial use, except that companies selling it as a hosted service need a separate licence. In Mistral's API it costs $0.70 per million input tokens and $2.10 per million output.
body:
Mistral AI published the weights of Mistral Large 4 on Hugging Face on October 29, after a public preview earlier in the month. The repository is mistralai/Mistral-Large-4-1T-A52B. It is the flagship model from the French company behind Le Chat, and one of the largest models anyone can download.

The model in numbers

Size: about 1 trillion parameters in a mixture-of-experts design, with about 52 billion active (49 billion per token, according to the model card).
Context: 1 million tokens.
Input: text and images; output is text. Mistral says it supports more than 160 languages.
Reasoning: one model for both instructions and reasoning, with Low, Medium and High effort settings.
Hardware: the deployment examples on the model card use 8 GPUs, and a quantized NVFP4 version is available for NVIDIA Blackwell GPUs.

Licence and price

The weights come under the Mistral Ecosystem Open-Weight License, a modified MIT licence. You can use, modify, fine-tune and sell products built on the model. The one condition: companies that offer the model itself as a hosted service need a separate commercial licence from Mistral.

If you would rather not host it, Mistral's API charges $0.70 per million input tokens, $0.07 for cached input and $2.10 per million output tokens. The model is also on OpenRouter, Microsoft Foundry and NVIDIA's hosted endpoints, and runs on vLLM and SGLang.

How it performs, according to Mistral

Mistral reports 48% on the Artificial Analysis Coding Agent Index, roughly tied with GLM-5.3 while using 47% fewer tokens per task, and 41% on Terminal-Bench 4.0, 13 points above the preview. These are the company's figures.

Who it matters to

Large 4 is for companies that need a frontier-class model on their own servers: for data that cannot leave the building, for European hosting, or for fine-tuning on their own material. For individuals, the API price is the more relevant number.

What this means if you are choosing an open model

If you already run open weights, such as DeepSeek, Large 4 is a new option to test, especially for multilingual and image-input tasks. Check the hardware first: a 1-trillion-parameter model is a data-centre deployment, not a laptop one.

If you plan to resell access to the model, read the licence: hosted-service providers need a separate deal with Mistral.
